text: But now, I sell the land, I collect 30 years of lease premium upfront, I spend it today.

speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
text: We can spend it over the next 30 years, as Ms Hazel Poa suggests, it is not an unthinkable proposition.

speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
text: We can put it away, invest it, spend the investment returns as we are doing, which is also sensible.

speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
text: But to say that we can take it forward and we can spend it and do not worry because in 30 years' time, we will get it back.

speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
text: Tell a banker, "In 30 years' time I'll pay you back.

speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
text: I borrow $1 from you, in 30 years' time, I'll give you back the hongbao".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, it is the same piece of land that is sold.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Every time it is sold, the land sale receipts go into the Reserves.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That is the only point I am seeking confirmation off from the Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
text: And that means the money which we are paying 30 years from now, today, has to be discounted by whatever interest rate the bank is charging, multiplied by 30 years.

speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
text: And the next one after that, maybe one cent for $1 and that series converges.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I was going to invite Mr Leong for the round-up, but I know he has run off for a short bio break, so, I would request everyone to just hold on for a while, because he is due to make his closing speech.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Leong, can I now invite you to make your closing speech?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Indeed, it is an honour for Hazel and myself.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: There has been a lot of discussion and debate on various topics.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We understand all the good things that the Past Reserves will bring to us and bring to our country, but what I want to emphasise today, is that all the good things that the Prime Minister, the Minister and other PAP Members have said will not go away even if we reveal our Reserves.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And it is right to reveal the Reserves to Singaporeans who are the rightful owners of the Reserves.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: People in the know, like myself, can make an estimate.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Just like any speculators, they can make an estimate from the data, from the statistics released by the Government.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We need to put Singaporeans, all of them, on the same page because we are all in this together.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, all the good things that the Prime Minister, the Minister and the PAP Members have said, they are not going to go away after we reveal our Reserves.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And the reasons, I will say afterwards again.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If some of the policies that PSP and WP have proposed are implemented – we have already said again and again.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Of course, the Prime Minister said, a little here a little there, we are going down the hole, be careful.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And with the wealth of knowledge and experience that the Prime Minister has, of course, we will take his advice very seriously.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But at the same time, we still think that for Singaporeans of today, there is a sense that they want to do better, but the environment is as such that they seem to be facing a lot of limitations.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, we are here, talking about better policies, than what the PAP is offering today.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: By the way, inflation, rising property prices, we can also say that part of it is attributed to the policies of the Government.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, we are talking about better policies here.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I hope in this Chamber, we can discuss and debate things, so that we can bring these better policies out and not keep saying that whatever the Opposition says, this is going to bring us down.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If you look at the details of the things, the policies, the opinions that PSP, and although I cannot speak every time for WP, those things that we are proposing.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Despite all the reasons I have given that it will not compromise the stability of our Singapore dollar and our economy.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Relying on the experience I have in the financial industry and also, based on my exchanges with Member Mr Liang Eng Hwa and the feedback from Members Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: First, I think the issue of defending our Singapore dollar against speculators and the issue of disclosing our Reserves are actually two different issues.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Because to defend our Singapore dollar against the speculators, first of all, the PAP Members had mentioned about the Hong Kong dollar peg, George Soros' attack on the Pound and all that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But they fail to point out that all these are what we call fixed exchange rate systems.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And of course, the speculators will attack the fixed exchange rate system when there is a mispricing.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But our Singapore dollar is essentially a float.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: As long as MAS runs its monetary policy properly, and we have full confidence in MAS, and makes sure our Singapore dollar value is in line with our economic fundamentals, that is the most important line of defence.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And of course, there are short-term speculators who may still come in to test and try their luck.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Then, our MAS today, I would say, have sufficient OFR to defend ourselves.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: How many countries in the world today have that?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In fact, there are other reasons why MAS have very good control over the forex market and control over the value of our Singapore dollar, but I would not go too much into that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, we have all the tools and the position and advantages to defend the Singapore dollar.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But to reveal the figure of our Reserve to the Singaporean is important for the Singaporeans to have full confidence without any other misconceptions.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That Singaporeans are the owners of the Reserves and they are entitled to the precise information of at least the financial reserves.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Even though the Budget and the Reserves are very technical topics that may not appeal to many Singaporeans, I have chosen to make many speeches in this House on these issues because they fundamentally impact our cost of living, quality of life, economic competitiveness, income equality and social cohesion.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: It is especially important in the past two years because the Government has made a number of tax increases that PSP thinks are not necessary.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Given the fact that Singaporeans are facing unprecedented problems in terms of cost of living and runaway property prices and, anyway, in our opinion at least our Budget and Reserves, we still have the leeway.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I also hope that by having more discussion on these issues, we can dispel the misconceptions and fake news relating to our Reserves.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Today, I do not think the majority of Singaporeans are really fully confident that we have over $1 trillion dollars of Reserves.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Because when we listen to some of the talk on the ground, they say, "If we have so much Reserves, why is the Government keeping our CPF savings?" I have to explain to them that, actually, these are two different issues.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: CPF savings are for your retirement, it has nothing to do with the fact that we do not have Reserves.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But this is a misconception, nevertheless, and we have to address that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Some fake news in the social media say Singapore has external debt that equals to 200% of our GDP.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: From the Government financial statements because we have total liabilities of about $1 trillion.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We must explain to Singaporeans that we have all these assets.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If not, the fake news will continue to be there.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And of course, all the rumours about the performances of GIC and Temasek, which I think are sometimes very unfair for the fund managers in those two organisations.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, I would like Singaporeans to have three takeaways from today's debate.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Ms Hazel Poa has explained two methods to calculate this based on the figures published by the Government in the Government financial statements.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: This $1.2 trillion, as I mentioned, will also continue to grow although the Prime Minister, the Minister and many Members have said that the rate of return on the financial reserves are not certain, not for sure.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But there are other sources of growth and, by the way, the 4% the Prime Minister mentioned about long-term investment growth, that is a standard assumption made by investment management entities.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And, of course, you can say that okay, in a few years' time the whole world will change but that 3% to 4% is based on a long-term forecast of the investment returns generated by these investment firms' forecast.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I mean, the actual track record of investment based on a universe of asset classes and this is a standard measure used by the investment firms worldwide.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, we can use 4% or maybe a bit more conservative 3%, but that is a reasonable number because as long as this world, this Earth is still intact, human beings will have economic activities and their economic activities will generate a return.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The cost can come in the form of higher taxes, higher property prices, higher cost of living or lower interest for CPF balances, depending on which of the five sources of growth the new Reserves come from.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Hence, the cost of accumulating Reserves has a direct impact on some of the top concerns of Singaporeans, such as the affordability of HDB flats, the rising cost of living, retirement adequacy, prospect for the younger Singaporeans and a host of other social ills.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: PSP also would like to continue to grow our Reserves at the current rate, if not for the fact that the heavy costs to Singaporeans are becoming more and more apparent, especially with the Government's tax increases over the last two years.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We have asked about the Reserves, we have asked about the land sales, NIR.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And the Government has said all cannot be used.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, today in my debate, I then said how about NIRC?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The NIRC also does not seem to be totally used for the benefit of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I mean, it is a matter of interpretation, but I pointed out that some of the NIRC has been locked up.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Some of the NIRC has been applied to very long-term infrastructure projects, including coastal and flood protection, all that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Coastal and flood protection – these are our existential problem.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Is this not an example that we should use our Reserves or some parts of the Reserves and not rely all this on the NIRC, which from the PSP's point of view, is supposed to enhance the welfare of Singaporeans so as to avoid the necessity to increase taxes.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Of course, we take that away, then we have to increase taxes.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is the message that Opposition has been presenting in this House.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We are just saying policies can be better.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: There is no tension between providing for present-day Singaporeans and continuing to provide for future generations – although hon Member Vikram Nair has cast doubts on that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But I have asked him that question on whether he knows how much Reserves we are accumulating each year and how much are our policies are going to spend, even at the very worst.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We are accumulating Reserves by the tens of billions.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Over the last two years, we are lucky.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: When there was a huge influx of capital into our country, the Government was able to accumulate an additional $250 billion additional Reserves over the last two years.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, with that, we are accumulating Reserves by tens of billions and we are proposing policies that spend at the very worst, very worst a few billion dollars.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Because not that we want to spend the money but present-day Singaporeans, many need the money especially the second half of Singaporeans in terms of income.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But this is not happening because the PAP Government was overly conservative fiscally and it has continued to raise taxes and fees which will maintain the current rate of reserve accumulation and, in exchange, giving out ad hoc handouts to appease Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is why we are confident that some of our policies, long-term policies, even implemented, will not lead to a big increase in the Budget because there are so many of these ad hoc schemes that we can actually integrate into some long-term scheme.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But we believe we have set aside too many resources currently and inadequate spending and investment and heavy overall taxes have weakened the present-day Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am sure Singaporeans will much prefer to be taxed less than receiving ad hoc handouts from the Government.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I hope this House today will appreciate that the PSP is not even asking for more NIR or land sales revenue for the Budget, at least for today we are not asking although we support all these policies.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: What we are saying today, is that even the NIRC has not been totally deployed for the full benefit of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And there is also this artificial deficit created by the current policy of charging land cost on HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: None of the policies that PSP recommended will weaken fiscal prudence and compromise our future ability to spend on any crisis that may come up in the future.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In fact, what our policies are aiming at is to increase our social cohesion, improve the conditions and the quality of life of Singaporeans, so that we have a stronger, present-day Singaporean Core and we can take crisis in our stride.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: A strong financial foundation is a good start.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: With the resources we have accumulated as a nation, we are confident that we can realise a new social compact together.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The 4G PAP leadership has presented a new social compact, Forward Singapore, which contains many invaluable insights from 200,000 Singaporeans on what kind of future Singapore they want.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We share Singaporean's aspirations to pursue fulfilment and contentment, instead of simply focusing on material needs.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: What is needed next are concrete policy prescription to realise their future.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: PSP thinks that financial freedom is the key to enabling Singaporeans to realise the aspirations they have articulated in Forward Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: When relieved of their financial burden, Singaporeans will be free to exercise their creativity, make their plans to realise their own potential and lead a happy life.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: As the most important way to enhance financial freedom for Singaporeans is to lower housing cost, PSP has tirelessly pushed for the Affordable Homes Scheme and Millennial Apartments Scheme to be implemented.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The raiding of Reserves allegation by the Government is just a distraction.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: PSP will continue to share with Singaporeans policies to facilitate a happy life and to ensure Singapore remains a secure place to live in, with rising incomes and good jobs for everyone, not just the rich and famous.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Today, many Singaporeans are struggling with their finances, even as Singapore becomes a paradise for the rich and famous, and sometimes the unscrupulous, like those in our recent money laundering case.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: After accounting for CPF contributions, this group of Singaporeans have very little left to save each month.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: It will be the right policy for the Government to start to relax its fiscal grip, which may reduce reserve accumulation slightly, but to offer more financial support to this group of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We should also be worried about the many social ills we are grappling with today, which can be traced back, at least partly, to financial difficulties.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The most important ones today are the low TFR and increasing mental health issues.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: A pre-conference poll shared by the IPS at the Singapore Perspective Conference last week found that high costs and stress were the top reasons for not wanting to have children across all age groups.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If the current generation of Singaporeans are struggling to maintain their standard of living, what incentive do they have to have children?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We acknowledge that the share of welfare spending in the Budget has increased significantly since 2011.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But these spendings do not address the root causes of the harsh economic realities faced by Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Ad hoc handouts do not change the structural economic realities that are faced by present-day Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: After receiving the temporary relief, they continue to be burdened by the rising cost of living and the prospect of having to downgrade from their current HDB flats in order to retire.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Without policy changes to address these structural economic issues, lower-income and even middle-class Singaporeans will become more and more dependent on Government handouts to survive.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: This is not the kind of future we want for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We must find other ways to improve the conditions of the Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: PSP wants all Singaporeans to benefit from our economic prosperity, not just the rich and famous.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: This is the future that PSP wants for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: To maintain that trust, the Government must now ensure that the Past Reserves are put to work for present-day Singaporeans to ensure that they can be competitive and lead a happy life in a globalised world.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The well-being of the current generation affects the ability of the future generations to thrive.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: A family that is constantly stressed by financial worries is not a good environment for children to grow up in.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: More than leaving behind national reserves to our future generation, it is more important to ensure that they are being brought up in a conducive family and social environment which allows them to develop the necessary skills to do well in the globalised world.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: PSP's policy proposals like the Affordable Homes Scheme and Millennial Apartments Scheme, are aimed at making our Past Reserves work harder for both the present-day generation and future generations.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We especially want to give the financial freedom to our younger Singaporeans to establish themselves quickly so that they can strive towards their ambition early in their lives.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: When this House supports this Motion, it will reaffirm that our Budget and Reserve accumulation policies should aim at laying the financial foundations for every Singaporean of every generation to achieve a life of fulfilment and contentment.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, Sir, the PSP tabled this Motion today to request two things from the Government on behalf of the people.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The total amount of our financial Reserves should not be a secret, because it is the hard-earned money of the people.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The Reserves have five main sources, including land sales revenue and investment returns of CPF deposits, all of which come from the people, especially considering that much of the land was acquired by the Government from our forefathers at low prices.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The total amount of our national Reserves also does not need to be a secret, as the Government has already disclosed a significant amount of financial information to comply with regulations from international organisations, such as the IMF.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: With this information, anyone, including foreign exchange speculators, can estimate the size of our Reserves.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Therefore, the Government's earlier portrayal of itself as a poor Ah Gong and the comparison of our vast reserves to "coffin money" is misleading.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: PSP urges the Government to be a responsible leader and disclose the total amount of our Reserves, allowing every citizen to use this information to assess our nation's fiscal and tax policies.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: With the investment returns from the Reserves each year, we will have sufficient financial resources to cope with the increased medical expenses resulting from our ageing population in the future.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Therefore, PSP strongly opposes the two consecutive increases in GST and property tax in 2023 and 2024.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: These two tax increases and the increase in the Government's fiscal surplus allow the Government to accumulate more Reserves, but they also seriously exacerbate inflationary pressures and increase the people's burden.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Therefore, the current predicament faced by the people is not solely due to external factors, such as the Ukraine war; the Government also bears some responsibility.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In addition, since 1985, the Government has been charging land costs to HDB.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: These costs have increased with the rise in property prices, leading to a significant increase in BTO prices.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: However, high BTO prices only absorb a portion of the land costs.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The remaining portion is subsidised by HDB, resulting in a deficit for HDB, which is ultimately borne by all taxpayers.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: PSP strongly urges the Government to waive the land costs for owner-occupied HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: This policy would allow every generation of young Singaporeans to realise their dream of owning a home at an affordable price around the age of 30.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Also, they would not need to sell their HDB flat in old age and would have sufficient CPF savings for retirement.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Without the lingering worry of repaying housing loans for years, the next generation of Singaporeans can boldly seize the opportunities brought about by globalisation, creating a better economic future for our country.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: PSP believes that a responsible Government and party should not solely pursue the maximisation of Reserves but should aim to maximise the happiness of the people.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: PSP will do everything in its power to persuade the Government and assist it in achieving this goal. : Mr Speaker, I beg to move.
